prior_limitation.content: Traditional bulk HEA preparation via vacuum arc-melting results in coarse grains and dendritic segregation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Bulk HEAs are usually prepared by vacuum arc-melting technology, with the disadvantages of coarse grains and dendritic segregation [ [3] , [5] ].

prior_limitation.content: The SPS consolidation of mechanically alloyed powders inevitably introduces interstitial elements leading to precipitated phases.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, it is inevitable that interstitial elements, such as O, N, etc. will be introduced during the preparing process, which will lead to the formation of precipitated phases [ [4] , [8] , [9] ].

causal_claim.content: Ti's high oxygen affinity compared to other elements leads to the formation of the TiO phase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It is apparent that Ti has a much higher oxygen affinity than other alloying elements, therefore leading to the formation of TiO phase

causal_claim.content: The finer grain size (1.35 μm) compared to the as-cast material leads to a strong grain boundary strengthening effect.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the equiaxed BCC matrix grains with the average grain size of 1.35 μm in the present work is much finer, therefore leading to a strong grain boundary strengthening effect

causal_claim.content: Precipitated TiO particles impede dislocation motion, increasing strength while slightly decreasing ductility.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the precipitated fine TiO particles are likely to impede the dislocation motion in the BCC matrix, thus increasing strength and slightly decreasing the ductility of the alloy

mechanism_principle.content: The excellent mechanical properties are attributed to solid solution strengthening, grain boundary strengthening, and precipitation strengthening from TiO particles.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles.

mechanism_principle.content: The formation of the BCC2 phase is attributed to slight inhomogeneity in alloying element distribution at grain boundaries.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: It can be speculated that the formation of BCC2 results from the slightly inhomogeneous distribution of alloying elements at the grain boundaries of sintered HEA

mechanism_principle.content: The retention of the TiO FCC structure is attributed to the rapid cooling speed after SPS preventing phase change to monoclinic.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The formation of TiO phase with FCC structure in the sintered sample indicated that the TiO phase remains in its original crystal structure at elevated temperature, due to the rapid cooling speed after SPS

hypothesis_statement.content: The solid solution sequence of elements during milling is related to their melting points, with lower melting point elements dissolving faster.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: It can be hypothesized that the solid solution sequence of the elements is related to the melting point, with low-melting-point elements being dissolved more quickly than the elements with higher melting points

evidence_result.content: XRD analysis confirms the presence of BCC structures after 40 hours of milling.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It confirms that the powders after 40 h of milling have only BCC structures

evidence_result.content: A new FCC phase is observed in the bulk HEA consolidated by SPS, contrasting with the BCC structure of the milled powder.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, a new FCC phase is observed in the bulk HEA consolidated by SPS, according to the XRD pattern shown in Figure 1 c

evidence_result.content: DSC analysis reveals an exothermic peak at 707.5°C, indicating phase transition during heating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 1 d presents the DSC curve that an exothermic peak is obviously observed at 707.5 °C

evidence_result.content: XRD patterns after heating at 900°C and in the consolidated bulk show new diffraction peaks characteristic of FCC structures.
evidence_result.evidence_span: new diffraction peaks, characterized as face-centered cubic (FCC) structures, are observed both in powders heated at 900 °C and consolidated bulk HEA

evidence_result.content: EDS analysis confirms the FCC precipitated phase consists of Ti and O with a 1:1 atomic ratio.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It is found that the FCC phase primarily contained Ti and O, with a Ti to O atomic ratio of approximately 1:1

evidence_result.content: The sintered alloy exhibits a compressive yield strength of 2709 MPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The alloy exhibits compressive yield strength of 2709 MPa
